newsitem.title: USA: U.S. provides more nuclear funds to Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: U.S. provides more nuclear funds to Ukraine.

text.p: The U.S. and Ukrainian defence ministers on Thursday signed an agreement for Washington to provide an additional $47 million to help Ukraine destroy former Soviet strategic nuclear missiles.

The deal completed at a Pentagon ceremony would add to $404 million the United States has already given to Ukraine, which last year completed the removal of all nuclear warheads from its SS-19 and SS-24 long-range missiles.

Defence Secretary William Cohen, at a news conference with Defence Minister Olexander Kuzmuk, praised Kiev's decision to become a non-nuclear state and said Washington would continue to help the former Soviet state modernise its military.
The funding, provided under the Nunn-Lugar Amendment approved by Congress, will help Ukraine complete destruction of the SS-19s themselves and begin planning destruction of the more modern SS-24s.
Kuzmuk and Cohen told reporters the U.S. secretary had agreed to visit Ukraine this summer.

"In 1993, Ukraine made a very bold and progressive choice -- it decided to dismantle its strategic nuclear arsenal. The people of Ukraine recognise that security comes from constructive alliances and not from nuclear weapons," Cohen said.
"Ukraine's commitment to nuclear disarmament is an inspiration to the rest of the world," he added of what had been the world's third biggest nuclear power after the breakup of the Soviet Union.
Kuzmuk said he had enjoyed visits earlier this week to U.S. bases.

"We have had a chance to talk to average Americans ... to live the life of the (U.S.) Marines, the Army, the Navy, the Air Force," he told reporters. "And I would like to tell you that the impressions that were formed during our 70 years of Soviet history, the impressions that we had of America, are gone with the wind right now."
The visiting minister, an army general, was asked if Ukraine stood by its decision not to seek membership in NATO.

"Ukraine has made a very clear statement that it is a neutral, non-bloc country and this is the political status of Ukraine right now," Kuzmuk replied. "But to answer your question, I would like to give it a little bit of a philosophical bent: There is nothing permanent in the past, in the present and in the future."
